He is a pretty hands-off professor. Piazza presence could be higher. He kind of expects you to figure a lot of stuff out, but it is totally manageable.

Overall, class is pretty easy.

He is actually not as bad as the reviews seem.

He is is a nice professor and tries to make the class interesting through EC participation and through jokes.

I would say to start the homeworks early, go to office hours if needed and prep ahead of times for the exams.

I got a 68% on the 2nd exam but did well on everything else and managed to get an A. 

He is nice but the class is very disorganized and the Piazza response times are poor.

I swear hes not that bad, would give 3.5 but rounding up to 4 seems fair

Pros:
EXCELLENT LECTURER (besides having bad slides) I learned so much from them
Didn't dive into the inner workings of the ML stuff which I appreciated, really focused on what you would use in the real world
Projects were interesting and pretty easily graded
Class itself is hard but its not hard to get a good grade
I liked the exams! instead of just cramming information for me to forget 2 hours after, I felt like I had to really understand the material to answer the questions

Cons:
Disorganized yes, this will be annoying
Exams are all over the place and vague
Sometimes would let us out of class early because he didn't plan lectures out well? This was annoying and felt like a waste of time

At the end of the day, hes a good lecturer who you will learn a lot from and its relatively easy to get a good grade. I really don't know what much else you can ask for, if you wanted to be spoonfed an A maybe take someone else but if you actually wanted to learn about DS/ML take Max

He's not bad, his lectures are sometimes interesting or hella boring. Some reviews say he's arrogant and condescending, but I didn't feel that. He's just so lazy. 

On the first day of class, his syllabus on the homepage added up to 97%. Then he had a slideshow where two back-to-back slides had 2 different syllabi, one adding up to over 100% and one to 100%.

His homework is put together lazily, the instructions are minimal, and there are mistakes like a link saying "SQL" leading to Pandas and a "Pandas" link leading to "SQL". 

He is not active on Piazza, and neither are his TAs, except for every week to announce that he's throwing up and office hours are cancelled. 

The first two exams weren't hard and the third one was hard. The harder the exam, the higher the grade, because any BS answer is marked as correct. Also, Exam 3 was not graded before the final. The final was not bad either, I struggled on the coding parts though, since they were a little tricky. The practice exams are kind of useless, like we were only given answers to half of the practice exams, and the answers are useless. I question like "name 3..." has the answer of "any 3 is fine", and some of the answers are like "take points off if they did xyz" instead of answering.

The homework is kinda fun, sort of. You get hella extra credit, so all the averages were above 100,% and there is hella extra credit outside of the homework. This class is literally just a free A.

Getting an A in this class is utterly trivial. None of the graded work is really that challenging, and there’s just such an insane amount of extra credit offered throughout the course that you’d honestly have to be pretty negligent to receive a low grade. Fardina is a very kind professor but I wasn’t really a big fan of the lectures–they were kind of boring and there were just way too many slides (much more than necessary to teach the material). Exams were pretty fair (though some questions were worded confusingly) and the final project does not take much time at all to meet the bare minimum requirements. 
Overall wasn’t the biggest fan of this course, but it was easy and gives a good overview of all the data science subfields.

Aishani's so nice!! She really enjoys helping people, and she does it well. She's also super approachable, so you're def in good hands if you have any problems.

Also, CMSC320 with Dr. Fardina is super informative, and the professor/TAs actually care about what students have to say.
I learned a lot and actually liked working on one of their homeworks (the detective one LOL).

great professor if you're looking for a an easy and low-stress cs course; i believe every homework and exam included a bonus section, and in addition, she provided a bonus homework and a couple of small "bonus quizzes" during class. i admittedly only went to lecture the first half-ish of the semester, and from what i could gather, fardina seems quite nice but imo her lecture style was rather boring. her slides are fairly detailed though, and her exams tended to ask more surface-level questions so between that and all of the extra credit she offered, her class was definitely a breeze

I really enjoy Dr. Alam's class! I've learned so much, and it’s made me seriously consider a future career in machine learning. The course covers a lot of material, but Dr. Alam keeps it engaging. She's super interactive, always responsive, very organized, and easy to talk to. I just wish she taught more upper-level CMSC courses!

I’m taking the summer session and just finished the final exam. The course was very well-organized—Dr. Alam posted slides and recordings regularly, which helped me stay on track alongside my internship. Piazza responses were quick and helpful. The content was engaging, and weekly quizzes made sure I kept up with the material. Overall, great class!

Fardina ftw. Absolutely goated. Took her over the summer and I’m the guy to slip every class so recorded lectures came in clutch and I learned a couple of stuff from this class since I’m new to ML stuff. She first covers data science principles - preprocessing stuff and then covers ML stuff for the rest of the class. Mostly high level overview with some math sprinkled in but it’s straightforward and easy. Also have a ton of extra credit points for the HW + additional opportunities. Ended the class with over a 100. She also cares about making sure students understand the material as well. Easy pick if you’re taking 320
I took this class over the summer. Very easy, very light grading, and very light workload.

I took this class over spring 2025 and if you want an easy grade, this class is definitely that, otherwise I think she is overrated. Her lectures are extremely boring and certainly confusing, making it hard to even warrant actually going to class. Is the material particularly hard? No, but her explanations most of the time end up making it more confusing than it should be. On the other hand, self-studying the slide material doesn’t work because the slides are severely bloated. 

The assignments in general are fairly straight forward and nothing on exams/homeworks/etc ever feels unfair. Although, if you are completing one of the homework assignments and have a clarifying question, don’t expect a response because TA’s will definitely not respond within 2-3 days and oftentimes leave questions completely unanswered. You can put almost no effort into this class and get at MINIMUM an A-. This class feels extremely unsatisfying as a whole.

She is a very sweet person, and she genuinely cares about her students' success. She makes the homework very doable and provides you with a ton of resources to learn data science materials. Her lectures were often smooth, and she presented the topics in a very clear and concise manner. I took her class over the summer, and it was very interesting, and it helped me develop a new perspective in data science and machine learning. I would definitely recommend her for CMSC320, and she is by far my favorite CMSC professor for her warm personality as well as her effort in teaching difficult concepts in lecture.

Super disorganized. Lectures are interesting but he forgets to plan them in advance. The actual material is very easy and you should be fine on exams (he tends to retroactively add a curve) and projects if you review slides or show up to class.

CMSC320 with Max

Lectures are interesting to begin with, and Max makes them entertaining as well. Couldn't have asked for a better early morning lecture (9:30 AM). 

Exams are on the harder side, but fair. He said once that if he could, he would replace exams with a one-on-one conversation with him just talking about the material (but obviously infeasible). The exams he gives attempt to replicate this vibe. 

Projects/Homeworks are really open ended, and honestly fun, (nothing like the highly specific, constraint ridden, edge-case-hell classes like 216 and 330). You are given data, and basically a single page of instruction of what he wants you to report on. You're free to be as extra, creative, or barebones as you want (being extra and creative often gets extra credit)

Overall a great change of pace from the rest of the CS meatgrinder classes and highly recommend

He's a funny and interesting lecturer, but also an extremely disorganized one. Many lecturers often are rushed through because he goes off on tangents, which, while interesting, they lead to speeding through challenging content. He also takes a long time to respond to emails and comes off as condescending. 

Exams are very challenging for two reasons: 
1. They can be difficult to prepare for. Since there are extremely abstract questions, you likely have never seen them before. Practice exams do not fully reflect what will be on the actual exam. They are sometimes unavailable and answer keys have incorrect/unclear answers. 
2. Questions often contain ambiguous language, making it difficult to understand what exactly is being asked. On one exam, a question was written so poorly that nobody in the class correctly answered it.

Overall, I would avoid taking this class with Max unless you absolutely need it. Save yourself the trouble and take it with Fardina.

Entertaining lecture, but a very disorganized lecture pacing. He assigned 7 of 3blue1brown's videos to look over instead of teaching such content himself. It doesn't seem to be optional videos either; it's the actual content that he will put on the exams. It felt very unprofessional. I would have learn a lot more if I had not gone to his class and spent the time studying on my own or with another professor. There is, however, alot of extra credit in class. You can take notes, group study photo, and submit it to Gradescope for extra credit. You could also put in more work on your homework to give extra credit. 

However, I would not take this class if your goal is to have a good start on the fundamentals of data science. As some of the comments said, he is an unserious professor; he is funny, but to learn, we would need to be more organized. I recommend only taking him if you already have prior machine learning, data science concepts and are here for a laugh.

This man confuses me. Everything people say about him is true and false at the same time. Even after getting to know the guy, he's still an enigma. 

Forewarning: DO NOT take this class at 9:30. You will fall into any of three categories if you do:
People who simply do not show up.
People who are consistently late and only get half of the information since the slides don't make up for the lecture.
Nerds. 
Lectures are entertaining enough, but Max knows that machine learning gets boring after a while. To solve this, he implements a no phone policy and instead keeps your attention with wacky stories about his work life (which are honestly pretty funny). However, most of the stuff seems to go one-ear-and-out-the-other for students (including me). Sometimes Max does do coding in lecture which, while being a nice break from the data science presentation slog, doesn't really help since he doesn't post any code he wrote.

I wish I could tell you what to do to study for exams and what to prepare for, but I cannot. Exams change at random between semesters, meaning you can have study material from someone from last semester's class and it wouldn't be any good. He always says to do the readings, and you should, but you cannot tell when they're important or not; some exams quite literally have 50% of the questions be reading-related questions (in which some were just trivia from the readings), while some exams will not have a single reading question on it. Regrades are pretty much a waste of time unless the TAs made a very obvious grading mistake. Minor grading mistakes will be justified with some hamfisted reason about how "you should've known this even though the question is marked open-ended" or "you had the right answer but added this phrase which I don't think it's correct", but I'm not sure whether that was Max or the arguably worse power-tripper TAs that handled the regrades. 

Homeworks are hard but graded leniently (as in points will be taken off for minor things but only 5 out of 100 points) to where the average is very high. Homeworks do get harder each semester though, so watch out for that.

In my opinion, you only want to take this course IF you have a light schedule. Don't take it concurrently with 351 and 330, and don't take it if you're doing other hard classes in the same semester. You will not want to spend time studying for this course, but you will have to, so make sure you have a clear schedule to do so.

Fardina kind of was terrible. The homeworks are easy but her lectures suck. Her slides are pretty overcomplicated and don't  have clear examples that I would've preferred to have to actually understand the material. She has a thick accent that I had trouble understanding and overall found it unengaging.

Her exams are the worst. No study guide apart from a giant google doc where she pasted what she covered in each lecture as if we didn't already know. No more than 3-4 practice problems given, most of the time either problems not on the exam or not enough problems to cover what was on the exam. Every midterm had to be extended by at least 10-15 minutes because nobody could finish her godawful exams within the HOUR AND 15 MINUTES we had allotted. The exam questions were also often in need of mid-exam corrections. For example, instructions were to evaluate a 3x3 kernel over a 6x6 matrix with stride=1. And to show every step of every matrix multiplication. Took me about 15-20 minutes. Only for a bit later in the exam where she announces you only have to show one step, despite the directions saying to show every single one. What a joke.

The previous reviews mention this class being an easy grade, and it could definitely be one but I definitely underestimated the amount of studying I needed to do for the exams because of how vague the information she gives is. 

Not to mention, not only does she give a final exam but also a final group project. Icing on the cake of a boring semester full of nonsense that completely pulled any interest or passion I had for data science away.

If you turn everything in on time and try at least somewhat on exams then you can do really well in the class. The homeworks/projects don't require you to write that much and usually everyone gets a good grade on them. The exams can be a little chaotic and not always that fair in my opinion but the grading is very lenient and you can earn a lot of half credit.The semester long group project is not that overwhelming and has been manageable.

He is a very nice guy that has great insight on many interesting tech topics. The class is structured alright. He posts slides, however sometimes goes off from the slides so it is important to go to lecture. His exams are on the medium-hard side. They are are about truly understanding the topics and not just memorizing the slides. Some of the questions tend to not be too specific causing more confusion. If you have a passion for data science or any of the topics taught then you will be fine. 

The homeworks are pretty open ended and the means are high. They are not too complicated. There is many opportunities to get extra credit. Answering hard questions, submitting photos studying with others, taking notes, and doing exceptionally well on homeworks and exams.

Overall, he is a great guy who you can tell cares deeply about the topics he teaches. This class is so great for learning about the real world applications of topics. If you put time into coming to lecture, doing the homeworks, and studying  well for the exams you will be able to get a B at the minimum.

This class is a very easy A, but her lectures are so boring. They don't really help with the homework, and they are so bad at answering questions on Piazza. The exams are also a little ridiculous, but she is super nice.

Eh. He's not terrible, but definitely not the most organized and reliable professor for logistics. He makes lectures entertaining (I heard the 9:30 class is pretty dead, but I'm in the 2:00pm), homeworks are graded leniently/weighted more than exams, and the workload is chill, honestly I was expecting a lot more. The only annoying part is studying for the exams with barely any provided study material.

there was like no context or descriptions for the projects/assignments. I would get points off for reasons that i didn't even realize were requirements. he also takes like 10 billion years to answer a piazza question and he doesn't even answer all of them. the content of the course was very disorganized, especially towards the end (he would add in random notes to himself in the middle of lecture), and for a lot of the content at the end there was no slides to refer back to so you had to pay attention and jot everything down in class or self teach. he goes through the slides he makes super fast too so you would have to go back after lecture and go through the slides yourself to take good notes. it also highkey felt like he did not care too much for our well-being; he said that he would make the second exam easier than the first exam but I remember walking out of the second exam feeling worse than the first one. I also think there was way too much emphasis on the really pretentious-sounding readings on exams. do not take max if you have a choice. people are gassing up how much he gives out extra credit but it is literally worth nothing in the grand scheme of your grade. all of the exam questions are SO VAGUE and the review questions he gives might be even more so. he will give us specific examples and applications of concepts on the exams that were not included in the review. and then at the end of the semester he has the audacity to ask us why we aren't understanding things....

A lot of previous points made are valid, but I believe they are exaggerated. I will say this is not an easy course, but putting in the work to understand topics will successfully prepare you for an entry level position or internship in data science. 

His exams are not liked because they require intuition and true understanding of topics discussed as opposed to the easier 'memorize and mind dump' of many other classes. Studying for his exams I will agree is difficult but I'd suggest giving AI the review he gives and other topics to generate open ended questions. These types of questions are the most prevalent and forces you to think outside of definitions and about real-world applications. He works to create fair exams and is willing to drop questions or apply a curve when necessary. 

This is why I believe attendance is mandatory. His slides are not conclusive and the ability to ask questions and answer them in person is one of the best ways to solidify understanding and earn extra credit. His lectures are entertaining and he speaks his mind. He is constantly looking to improve his lectures semester by semester due to how fast the subject is changing, so content and topic tend to change based on what is relevant today. I will not tolerate all the Max hate here. I genuinely looked forward to my 9:30am lectures.

I HIGHLY recommend taking this class if you're interesting in learning about data science and being prepared for data science interviews. 

His exams are very much pulled from what those interviews could be. I studied by taking notes on things that didn't make sense the first time I learned them, until they made sense, over and over and it has worked. I feel like a lot of people tried to study using practice exams, but that's not super helpful since his exams are different from one another. Practice exams in this course should be more like a last checkpoint / once over before the exam, not a sole study tool. 

These were probably the most entertaining lectures I've ever been to. Max is also a super nice, thoughtful, and funny person who is clearly trying very hard to help us. He takes time to explain why he's structuring the course in the way that he does during class. He even added an assignment at the end structured for us to be able to put it as an impressive project on our resume.

The assignments were super open ended and you could do the bare minimum and get an 100. If you have extra time and want to really commit, you'll get a bunch of EC for the extra stuff you do. 

All in all, my favorite class and prof at UMD. I feel like I got more prepared during this class for the job market than any other course. I loved how he taught us such modern AI models and adjusts the curriculum to new innovations. Really appreciate this course. Would recommend to anyone.

literally the best. if you want an easy a, don't take max. if you want to learn the concepts, take max. he's so nice and chill. exams grades are a little low but the hw counteracts that easily. take him!

Max is probably the most interesting lecturer that I’ve had within the CS department at UMD. As somebody with a chronic class-skipping problem, I found myself only missing one or two of his lectures. His exams are tougher than most, but the grade distribution balances out such that his class is very passable without doing well on them, and the vision behind his questions is one I can understand, as he is actively trying to teach his students applicable material to a professional job and not just formulaslop.

Take this class for the plot but not if you actually want to learn anything. I don't understand how Max had some level of success in the industry as he literally didn't understand that not all data that is bell curved shaped is a normal distribution(among many other obvious things). It was entertaining to watch him be confused and say the most out of pocket things("A human life is worth $2000. If I donate $2000 every year I can do whatever I want because I've already contributed positively")

Homework's were time consuming but interesting and probably good practice. Exams were poorly written and poorly graded(got 5-10% on every exam via regrade request). They were hard not because they tested tough concepts or required an in depth knowledge to do well but just because they attempted to ask you a very specific thing vaguely but ended up doing it weirdly. Advice: do really well on the HWs. Extra credit is awarded for extra long reports, pretty reports and using concepts not discussed in class so make an effort to do these things on your report. Getting a 110% or higher on an assignment worth almost as much as an exam will allow you to do pretty poorly on the exams and still do well in the class.

Also do the readings closely. He asks pretty specific questions on the exams.

It's hard to review him because there is so much good and bad about him. If you go to lectures, he'll explain stuff really well and he's super considerate and nice, but there'll be just random moments where its like hes looking at his own slides for the first time in years. That was kinda annoying, but its eh. 
The homeworks are super easy, I think the median for all of them was 100. They feel like easy points, and the instructions are super vague, so it kind of lets you have room to do whatever, as long as its clear you took something away from it. I thought they were way better the coding assignments you would get in like 330 where its just follow the instructions and code it. 
As for the exams, he makes a point about how theyre supposed to test your understanding of the material rather than how well you memorized it, but I honestly didn't feel that. Just study for the first exam to get a feel for what the questions are like, because his exam writing style is very unique

Max is an INCREDIBLY lazy professor. It truly feels like he puts in 0 time to preparing for lectures because his slides are often incomplete or a mess, he doesn't know the answers to any questions students ask during class (or he gives the vaguest hand-wavy response), and he frequently ends lecture 30 minutes early because he's run out of things to say. It feels like he himself doesn't fully understand what he's teaching sometimes. Like the other reviews note, he also fills a bunch of lecture time with unrelated thoughts and work stories, and while the class seems to find them entertaining (and Max loves the attention and reactions he gets from saying all his unpopular or taboo things), it would be better if there was more real content time to match. Max doesn't believe in studying any of the data science concepts rigorously, and while teaching a survey of topics at a high-level could be acceptable, he doesn't even touch on enough topics to make the class worthwhile. Instead, we learn in an entire semester basically what someone could get from reading a few articles on data science for a few hours. He also assigned multiple hours worth of youtube videos this semester in lieu of teaching the topics himself, and made the content directly testable on the exams. His reading-based exam questions (which constitute a significant portion of each exam grade) are genuinely trivia and not relevant to any fundamental understanding of data science concepts. He isn't active in responding to people's concerns on Piazza, mistakes are abundant in his posted materials, and policies seem to change frequently (such as him announcing a flat 11% curve on exam 1 then never following through on it). Overall I find it difficult to give a higher rating to a professor who transferred such little knowledge to his students and put in such little effort into his full-time teaching job.

I excelled in this class (and you definitely can too) by always going to lecture, reviewing the slides carefully before exams, memorizing major points from the readings, and thinking critically about what Max must be looking for while answering exam questions.

PROS:
- Very funny and engaging professor, I was rarely bored during lecture and actually liked going.

- Homework assignments make up a great portion of the grade, making it easier to pass even if you slip up on an exam.

- HW assignments are very interesting despite being vague. He might ask something like "here's a dataset, write me a report about the data," and it's up to the student to decide what to do from there. A lot of extra credit is given for creativity, effort, and generally impressing the grader, which helps boost your grade at the end of the semester.

- Exam questions could pop up in data science interviews. They also force you to be well-prepared and understand the content.

- Homeworks can be decent projects to put on your resume

- Max is a pretty reasonable professor and is willing to help out, as long as you talk to him well ahead of deadlines. 

- Sometimes cancels class spontaneously, but this could also be perceived as a con since the class might fall off schedule

- He gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities. I would say to do all of them; you might end up needing it at the end of the semester. Lots of it doesn't even take that long, it just involves you submitting notes for a lecture or taking a photo of you studying for an exam with a friend. 

CONS:
- While he can be really unserious, some people might not like that style, since it can lead to distraction or falling off schedule

- Exams are pretty hard and can sometimes be very poorly worded. Class averages for the first two midterms were not great (Exam 1 was roughly 66%, Exam 2 was 70%)

- He can be pretty disorganized. Either he forgets to cover something in class, or just doesn't cover it at all since he spent too much time in class going on random tangents. 

- He takes pretty long to respond to emails.

- You will need to do a lot of self teaching. He covers a little bit of pandas, but aside from that, not much code is covered at all. I had to teach myself how to use more pandas functions, Scikit-learn, and other important frameworks necessary for class.

Other notes/takeaways:
- Watch the 3Blue1Brown playlist on neural networks when you get to that part of the class, those were really helpful in understanding the concepts. Those concepts are also testable.
- Start homework early to avoid late submission or cheating.
- Do all the extra credit opportunities, they really don't take that long to do and could really help you out.

Overall, he's a decent professor and I enjoyed taking the class with him.

Max has roughly 20 years of experience as a data scientist prior to teaching and everything he does in class (exams, homework) is geared toward preparing someone to work in the industry, which is something I really appreciate. I think the reviewer who said "Overall a great change of pace from the rest of the CS meatgrinder classes and highly recommend" was very accurate. I'd highly recommend taking 320 with Max for this reason. (I can see why something like 250 or 351 might be awkward with him, though, since that's not his passion.)
Exams are somewhat difficult but are not a huge portion of your grade individually. Homeworks are designed to mimic real-world data science assignments and are decent resume fodder, and in terms of grading, are easy 100s to boost your grade. Extra credit is also available for homeworks if you put in extra effort.
As many other reviewers mention, he is disorganized, but I still found his lectures to be entertaining and educational. I would recommend attending his lectures as he deviates from his slides a lot.

If you just want the credit, by all means, I see no reason to dissuade you. The homeworks are long, but you have plenty of time. The exams are overall pretty fair, and the group project is a fine opportunity to do research on something you're genuinely interested in. However, I cannot in good conscience recommend this professor due to the heinous amount of AI-generated material passed off as course materials.

There are small slights everywhere, from the cover image of the syllabus being a blatantly AI-generated mess to convoluted, substance-lacking paragraphs hitting every AI red flag scattered throughout the supplemental material she "wrote" herself, but my least favorite of them is the class slides. There are two lecture slides that both have what are clearly screenshots of ChatGPT-generated text slapped on. One of them has black squares covering the fact that the headers start with 4.1 4.2 4.3, which implies she generated a lot more content than she showed and could have just hid it better, and using it to any extent breaks trust and brings into question all of her lecture material, but I digress.

It's possible you don't have as visceral a hatred for artificial intelligence as I do, especially if you're taking a class on data science, but if you think, as I do, that lecture content in a college course that you pay money for should not be a bunch of AI-generated bullet points read back to you, I would suggest looking for another professor. Hopefully, one of your alternatives has a different stance regarding the use of AI in teaching.

The goat

Super lenient on grading and is funny and entertaining in lecture. I really enjoyed the loose homework style with few guidelines, especially HW4 where you make a slide deck.

Max continue to be silly

He will make you truly love data science. However, his exams tend to be quite challenging. Fortunately, there are many opportunities for extra credit through homework assignments to help balance that out. If you take his class, be sure to give your homework your best effort since it is open-ended, and pray about the exams. I managed to score a 66% on one of his exams, but I ended up with an A in the class thanks to my hard work on the homeworks.

This is the first time I felt like I walked away from a class with genuine real world skills, and this is exactly what Max aims for. This class is completely what you make of it. If you do the bare minimum and want a free A from an elective, avoid. If you want to become a better Data Scientist, Max's course will take you to the next level. To me, the lectures felt like YouTube videos and I walked away having learned something new after every lecture.

Max is very different from lecturers we are used to. He makes his exams extremely difficult to make you truly understand concepts instead of memorizing, but they get curved and you have a lot of opportunity for extra credit to make up for them. 

Tips to succeed: 
- go above and beyond on the projects and get creative with it, Max will give you a lot of extra credit and lets you put them on your resume
- do every reading Max assigns and know the core concepts of them before exams, he'll ask related questions
- expect really difficult exam. use the practice exams purely to test your knowledge rather than learn from. Much of the learning for me was watching YouTube videos to better visualize the concepts.
- do NOT take if you're not interested in data science, but if you are, 320 with Max will be the best class you'll take in college
- Attend lectures, they're super entertaining and gives you hints on the exams

I had the 2 PM lecture for this class, and it was the best decision I've ever made. His lectures are entertaining at times, and he's probably one of the funniest professors here at UMD. But I honestly don't think he should be teaching at all. He has a great knowledge of data science, but this was a class I was really looking forward to taking, and was really interested in the content, but Max, as the professor, was a big no. He doesn't know how to teach and is probably one of the laziest professors here. His exams are pretty hard, and he doesn't help you with review. He posts these like weekly recaps, but they are kind of useless because they are vague about what you should know. His practice exams are nothing close to his actual exams, so they are just useless. Homeworks were not that hard, and he gave a lot of time to complete them, which was great. But honestly, I barely learned anything from him and really had to teach myself everything. Max is a great guy, but he is not suited to be a professor.

Okay, he's a very divisive professor. I think the upshot is that if you're genuinely passionate about the material, you'll absolutely find him to be a 5/5. If you just want an easy time, take Fardina.

PROS:
- Lectures are extremely entertaining
- Lots of opportunity for extra credit on the homeworks which will SAVE your grade, if you know what you're doing
- Just a chill guy to talk to (if you're passionate about Data Science or CS or probably anything remotely you share in common, just yap to him in OH and it'll be a blast. He's happy to help for interview prep and stuff)
- Puts in an INSANE amount of work to maximize grades and give back points for stuff/curve grades up
CONS:
- If you don't know what you're doing, then this class is going to be REALLY damn hard. Exams can be brutal, which more than offsets the lenient grading I described above. My A+ is only because homework EC saved me
(To be real, I think this is where most of his bad reviews come from)
- Had to cancel class more than a few times because of a medical condition? I don't know exactly. I'm not sure how much of an impact it had because I feel as though we got through most if not all the material we needed to, but it did mean he had to throw out a project.


I can understand where his bad reviews come from... but I personally found this to be an easy class, and absolutely think that he deserves a much higher rating (2.8 at time of writing). One of my favorite professors, if not my absolute favorite.

Maks is a pretty interesting professor who brings up important ideas that make you think deeply about the topics during lecture. Unfortunately, this also extends to his approach to exams. Your grades on exams are not dictated by how well you study or pay attention to the lectures but instead by how well you understand data science. This may sound fair but when you apply that to an intro course, you are getting taught basic ideas and then expected to extrapolate from that like a career data scientist (he even takes questions from data science interviews). Every question on his exams is a trick question. These questions are often poorly worded (doesn't clearly indicate what it's looking for) or straight up impossible (he had to take a couple of these off the exams). This can be a fun challenge if you have a light semester, but if you have a really heavy schedule, it becomes a nightmare of bashing your brains against the material hoping something sticks. If you are thinking about being a data scientist, this is the course for you. Taking this course tests your resolve and tells you if you actually want to be a data scientist. I thought I wanted to be a data scientist but this course showed me that I had a bright future in creative writing. Although, after a semester of getting straight Cs on exams and bombing homeworks, I still ended up with a B so he's a pretty understanding grader.

Lectures are chaotic and uninformative, but because of how bad the slides he posts are, you have to go to them to learn the material. Exams had low scores, as 1 midterm and the final had a C- median and 1 midterm had a D median for my section. The questions aren't hard because there are gymnastics involved, they are hard because you get very little exam review material and because most topics are only mentioned offhandedly in the slides, but given conceptual questions on the exams. I would highly recommend completing the homework before the midterm that covers the corresponding topics, as the hw is the best (and only) way for you to examine the material better than in lecture. 
He gives substantial opportunities to improve your grade through extra credit. The bulk of extra credit opportunities are on the hw assignments. Be warned however that even though it is "extra", he considered all of the hw extra credit before he decided on a curve, diminishing the curve to the point that unless you scored an A average on exams, extra credit is almost required to achieve a high grade.

He assigned 4 homeworks, all of which were very easy. Normally he just gives extra credit for the vague criteria of a submission being high effort or impressive. Sometimes though he announces specific additions that he will give extra credit for in class. When you consider how easy the homework assignments were, getting the substantial extra credit to give yourself a good shot at an A requires the same amount of effort as the hw for a typical cs class. For each hw, about half of the class got extra credit.

I really liked this course. Fardina is super nice and genuinely cares about her students. I interacted with her a lot during class and also asked many questions after class and she was always patient and took the time to help me understand what I was trying to do. The homework was straightforward and helpful. The midterms were a bit long, but the final exam was very doable and fair. Overall, it was a great experience for me and I learned a lot.

I really loved CMSC320! The homeworks were interesting and helped me learn a lot. If you take this class, you willll notice that Fardina is very warm and always willing to help. she takes the time to answer students questions, even after class.

Max is a funny guy. While his lectures weren't useless, he wasn't a great lectuerer and doesn't have great slides, and you aren't missing out on too much if you miss them. Honestly, if you only care about the content, you would probably be better off just watching some youtube video on each of the topics. He even replaced some of his lectures with youtube videos when he was sick.
He has a whole philosophy of not testing people just memorizing content, but then makes exams that basically require memorization. Because of this, he doesn't post good review materials for exams, which makes studying for them really tricky. He also makes you do outside readings and puts questions about them on the exam.
Homeworks (which are projects) weren't that hard and are graded pretty leniently, but he doesn't teach you how to do them, you have to look for resources online. They are worth 40% of your grade, and he offers a lot of extra credit by putting extra effort into homeworks which somewhat makes up for the harder exams.

He seems like a hit or miss for most people. Some people don't really vibe with the way he runs the class, and I was one of them. Even still, I wouldn't say he's bad enough to put off a semester to get a better teacher.

I pleasantly enjoyed his class last semester. The lectures were interesting and none of the assignments were that challenging just took some time to make sure you hit all the requirements. He also would give lots of extra credit on the homework assignments for doing just a little more than the bare minimum which helped out a lot as some of the exams were a little tricky. Overall hes a great professor and the long you do the readings and understand them before the exam the exams wont be that hard and then make sure you are actually putting effort into the homeworks and this class won't be that hard.

name: CMSC320
title: Introduction to Data Science
description: Prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CMSC216 and CMSC250. Restriction: Permission of CMNS-Computer Science department. Credit only granted for: STAT426 or CMSC320. An introduction to the data science pipeline, i.e., the end-to-end process of going from unstructured, messy data to knowledge and actionable insights. Provides a broad overview of several topics including statistical data analysis, basic data mining and machine learning algorithms, large-scale data management, cloud computing, and information visualization.
